image.alt: A Marble Queen Pothos with heart-shaped leaves marbled in cream-white and green, trailing from a white pot

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but the white fades

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; spreads fast, so keep it trimmed

home_use.note: Trails well from a shelf near a bright window

snap: A trailing vine with heart-shaped leaves marbled in cream-white and green, with a different pattern on every leaf. It is easy to keep and forgives a missed watering, but it needs brighter light than other pothos to hold its colour. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The pothos is native to the Society Islands in the South Pacific and now grows wild across the tropics, where it climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. The Marble Queen is a cultivated form whose green leaves are heavily streaked with creamy white. Indoors the vines trail 2 m or more, or climb a pole or trellis. It grows a little slower than the plain green pothos.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light to keep the white marbling. In dim light the leaves turn greener, and direct sun scorches the white patches. Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, and never leave the pot standing in water. It droops when thirsty and perks up soon after a drink. Yellow, mushy leaves mean too much water.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The marbling runs from fine green flecks on cream to broad green streaks, and no two leaves match. If a shoot comes back all green, cut it back to a marbled node so the pattern doesn't take over. Cuttings with a node root easily in a glass of water. Trim the tips to keep it full, and give it a moss pole to climb for larger leaves.
